To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the large firm has become the dominant form of enterprise in the industrial economies of the world and that the largest firms are found in the capital- and energy-intensive industries whose products are marketed on a large scale.

(1) in all four countries there was a small number of firms that dominated the largest 100 firms, (2) in the United Kingdom, as in the United States but not in Germany or France, there was a significant number of large firms in the textile and clothing industries, (3) in all four economies the largest firms were found primarily in capital- and energy-intensive industries whose products are widely distributed, (4) the largest firms tended to be in the same industries,

the largest industrial firms in all four countries are found primarily in the same groups of industries and that the largest firms are larger in the United States than in the other three countries and have been larger for a longer period of time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the growth of large-scale enterprise in four major European countries and the United States.
the growth of the large industrial enterprise in a period in which the world was being industrialized and in which the world market for many industrial products was expanding.
the growth of the large industrial enterprise in a number of countries, with the United States and United Kingdom as the principal subjects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the large-scale industrial enterprise has become a major economic force in all four countries.
in the period from 1920 to 1950 the United States and Britain experienced a common trend toward a more concentrated and integrated industrial structure.
the growth of the modern transnational corporation in the United States is the outcome of a unique historical process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in all the countries studied there was a marked increase in the number of large firms in the period after World War I.

the large industrial firm, in the sense of a large, capital-intensive, and technologically sophisticated enterprise, is an Anglo-Saxon phenomenon. The United States has had the most, and the United Kingdom the next

the growth of the transnational industrial firm in the United States was more rapid and more extensive than in the United Kingdom, and that the growth of such firms in the United States occurred earlier than in Britain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the United States was the most hospitable environment for the growth of the large industrial enterprise, but the reasons for this are complex.
the rise of large firms was the product of the same forces in the United States as in the other three countries.
the growth and spread of the modern large-scale industrial enterprise has been an international and not a national phenomenon.
